Junior Cybersecurity Associate
HTB Certified Junior Cybersecurity Associate (HTB CJCA) is a highly hands-on certification that assesses the candidates’ cybersecurity assessment skills. HTB Certified Junior Cybersecurity Associate holders demonstrate foundational technical competency across both offensive and defensive cybersecurity domains. They are equipped to identify common vulnerabilities, perform basic (post-)exploitation, and recognize potential security gaps. They are also capable of conducting SIEM-assisted security monitoring, analyzing network traffic and logs, and detecting intrusions. With hands-on experience in these areas and a hybrid skill set, they can assess and report on security issues in enterprise environments.

HTB Certified
Active Directory Pentesting Expert
HTB Certified Active Directory Pentesting Expert (HTB CAPE) is a highly hands-on certification assessing candidates' skills in identifying and exploiting advanced Active Directory (AD) vulnerabilities. HTB CAPE certification holders will possess technical competency in both internal and external AD and Windows penetration testing, understanding complex attack paths, and employing advanced techniques to exploit them. HTB CAPE certification holders will demonstrate proficiency in executing sophisticated attacks abusing different authentication protocols such as Kerberos and NTLM and abusing misconfigurations within AD components such as ADCS, WSUS, Exchange, and Domain Trusts. Furthermore, they will be adept at leveraging specialized tools to exploit AD from Linux and Windows and utilizing Command and Control (C2) frameworks for post-exploitation operations.

HTB Certified
Wi-Fi Pentesting Expert
The HTB Certified Wi-Fi Pentesting Expert (HTB CWPE) is designed for professionals seeking to master real-world Wi-Fi exploitation. Through a rigorous, hands-on assessment, candidates demonstrate their ability to attack and compromise wireless networks across all major protocols, including WPA3 and WPA-Enterprise. HTB CWPE certified experts are skilled in deploying rogue access points, harvesting credentials, bypassing captive portals, exploiting routers and leveraging advanced tools to penetrate even hardened enterprise wireless environments. Using industry standard tools such as Airgeddon, Eaphammer, Kismet, Wifipumpkin3, Bettercap, and Aircrack-ng, candidates learn to exploit vulnerabilities across WEP, WPA, WPA2, WPA3, and WPA-Enterprise networks. Beyond wireless compromise, CWPE professionals are also capable of pivoting into internal networks and gaining an initial Active Directory foothold by exploiting weaknesses in enterprise Wi-Fi networks.

HTB Certified
Offensive AI Expert
HTB COAE is a hands-on certification assessing knowledge gained by a curriculum co-developed with Google on identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities in AI and ML systems. Certification holders demonstrate competency in adversarial machine learning, LLM prompt injection and jailbreaking, LLM output exploitation, AI application and system security, AI defense, and AI privacy. The curriculum aligns with Google's SAIF, the OWASP ML Security Top 10, OWASP Agentic Top 10, and OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025. Holders can also conduct professional AI red-team assessments and write client-ready reports.

HTB Certified Detection Engineering Principal (HTB CDEP) is an advanced, practical, scenario-based assessment designed to validate learners’ ability to apply detection engineering concepts in real-world enterprise environments. The candidates will work across areas including Windows and Linux telemetry, process and memory activity, API and callstack analysis, low-level detection opportunities, analyzing suspicious binaries and debugging the execution flows, identifying relevant attack techniques, and developing robust detection logic.
